doc.title: Tools and Applications
doc.paragraph: This section describes the various tools and executables that come with Adaptive Framework.

section.title: afw
section.paragraph: This is an executable command-line tool that provides an interactive way to run Adaptive expressions, scripts, templates, and test scripts, and a "local" mode used by the AFW Python and Perl adaptive function bindings.
Its options, syntaxes, and local mode protocol are in the afw reference: afw Usage (the same text as afw --help).

section.title: afwfcgi
section.paragraph: FastCGI is a binary protocol for interfacing interactive programs with a web server. FastCGI was created to provide a more efficient alternative to traditional CGI by reducing overhead. The afwfcgi application is a FCGI (FastCGI) application that starts up and processes FCGI requests. These requests can originate from a FCGI client, or be proxied by a popular web server, such as Apache or Nginx. The afwfcgi executable takes the following command-line arguments:

row.column: Specifies the configuration file to use. Default: afw.conf in the working directory.
Specifies where to listen for FastCGI connections: a file path for a Unix domain socket, or :port for a TCP port. Default: :9345.

Specifies the number of request threads to start. Default: 1. Stack size follows application configuration threadStackBytes when set; otherwise the larger of 2MiB, four times limitCStackHeadroomBytes, and the process stack limit (ulimit -s). A typical 8MiB process stack limit yields 8MiB per thread. The afw command uses the process stack.
Loads an extension prior to starting. May be repeated.
Specifies the content-type to use for the configuration file. Default: json, which accepts relaxed JSON.

section.paragraph: On SIGTERM or SIGINT, afwfcgi stops accepting new requests, lets each request thread finish the request it is processing, removes its Unix domain socket and exits. Work that would take a long time, such as a large retrieve, checks for the stop as it goes and ends early with error terminating (HTTP 503), so the process does not outlive the grace period its supervisor gives it. The afw command treats the same signals as a request to stop the work it is doing.
